task.description: Design a fix for GH #520 / ISS-0186: TC-EXP-301-05 (tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig, block starting ~line 570) asserts on a measured wall-clock delta between two separate database reads (next_attempt_at read BEFORE markRetry, then read AFTER, subtracting to get observed_delta_ms, compared against expected_ms +/- 500ms tolerance at lines 689-694). Root cause: Queue.markRetry (src/effects/queue.zig:84-108) computes next_attempt_at = NOW() + $3::interval entirely on the PostgreSQL server side using SQL NOW() -- the Zig test has no control over or synchronized view of that server clock, and under ~20-test-binaries-concurrent load (zig build test-integration-svc), scheduling jitter between the test's two separate query round-trips exceeds the +/-500ms tolerance. Design a fix that asserts a deterministic property instead: read next_attempt_at AND a server-side NOW() snapshot in the SAME query (single round-trip, e.g. SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM next_attempt_at)*1000, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW())*1000 in one statement, executed once, immediately after markRetry returns) so there is no cross-round-trip jitter window at all -- the interval between next_attempt_at and that same query's NOW() should equal the requested backoff_ms exactly (modulo query execution time within a single round trip, which is sub-millisecond, not the multi-hundred-ms cross-request jitter the current two-round-trip design is vulnerable to). Alternatively/additionally consider asserting the raw interval algebraically: since next_attempt_at = t_exec + backoff_ms where t_exec is the server's own NOW() at execution time, capturing BOTH values in one query removes the wall-clock-relative-to-test-process measurement entirely. Read the current test block in full (tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig around lines 567-696) and src/effects/queue.zig's markRetry before designing. The acceptance criteria require the assertion still fails on a genuine backoff-schedule regression -- do not weaken it into a tautology (e.g. do not just assert next_attempt_at > NOW() with no bound).
acceptance_criteria: Design replaces the two-separate-query wall-clock delta measurement with a single-round-trip deterministic assertion
The assertion still fails if the backoff schedule regresses -- not weakened into a tautology
Design is implementable as a test-only change (tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig) with no production code touched
No implementation code present in the design artefact

result.summary: Designed a test-only fix for GH #520 / ISS-0186 (TC-EXP-301-05 flaky backoff assertion). Replaces the two-separate-round-trip wall-clock delta (next_attempt_at read before markRetry, then after, subtracted) with a single combined SELECT that reads next_attempt_at and server NOW() in the same statement execution immediately after markRetry returns, comparing next_attempt_at - NOW() against expected_backoff[i] with a tightened 50ms tolerance (down from 500ms). The before-read is removed entirely except a minimal attempt_count-only pre-check retained for the dead-letter branch condition. The assertion remains non-tautological -- it still bounds against each of the four distinct expected_backoff values, so a genuine markRetry interval regression still fails the test. No production code changes.
